title: AmbientFM: A Foundation Model for Ambient Sensing
claim: One shared backbone is pre-trained on unlabeled real-world signals with complementary self-supervised objectives, then lightly adapted to many downstream tasks.
layout: 3 numbered stages left-to-right on top, 3 objective panels below
description: A wide two-tier figure. The top row has three numbered stages. Stage 1, In-the-wild Wi-Fi Data Collection, shows photos of commercial devices and a house cartoon with a router, an edge device and a person. Raw CSI appears as stacked sheets that become a green-yellow spectrogram, the processed CSI. Stage 2, Pre-training, is a green-outlined chain of blocks: Adaptive Frequency Aggregation, Linear Proj., Transformer Encoder (6 layers) and Sequence Rep. Stage 3, Task Adaptation, is a list of colored task names with icons: fall detection, localization, activity recognition, user identification, gesture recognition and imaging. The bottom row, titled Pre-training Objectives, has three panels: contrastive learning with WiFi-tailored augmentations and an NT-Xent loss, masked channel reconstruction with an encoder-decoder and MSE, and a physics-informed ACF loss with an autocorrelation plot. The eye goes first to the colorful spectrograms and the top pipeline.
caption: AmbientFM overview. AmbientFM pre-trains a shared sensing backbone on in-the-wild CSI with complementary self-supervised objectives, then adapts it to diverse downstream tasks with lightweight tuning.
abstract: Ambient intelligence seeks to continuously understand human presence, activity, and physiology in physical spaces, enabling smart environments, health monitoring, and human-computer interaction. WiFi infrastructure offers a ubiquitous, always-on, and privacy-preserving sensing substrate across billions of IoT devices. Yet ambient sensing with WiFi remains largely fragmented, with most systems relying on task-specific models, labeled data collection, and customized training pipelines. We present AmbientFM, a foundation model for ambient sensing through ubiquitous WiFi signals. AmbientFM is pre-trained on 9.2 million unlabeled Channel State Information (CSI) samples collected over 439 days from 20 commercial device types deployed in real homes, the largest real-world WiFi CSI pre-training corpus reported to date. It learns transferable wireless representations through contrastive learning, masked reconstruction, and physics-informed objectives tailored to wireless signals. With lightweight adaptation, a single backbone transfers to 9 downstream tasks, achieving above 0.90 AUROC on all classification benchmarks and supporting dense spatial reconstruction. AmbientFM reduces the need for labeled data and task-specific design, enabling scalable ambient intelligence on existing wireless infrastructure.
